investigation_quality.expected_solution: Investigation must enumerate the modules in the cycle: src/flask/__init__.py → src/flask/json/__init__.py → src/flask/globals.py → src/flask/app.py. Root cause: Circular import between flask.json and flask.globals when flask.json is imported at module level before Flask app is initialized. INVESTIGATION.md must capture the cycle, the trigger import, and propose a workaround without changing code in this phase.
evaluation_criteria: Must enumerate every module participating in the cycle
Must identify the trigger import (the symbol whose load resolves the cycle)
Must include severity / workaround language without prescribing the actual code change

cycle_identified.expected_solution: The import cycle is: src/flask/__init__.py → src/flask/json/__init__.py → src/flask/globals.py → src/flask/app.py → src/flask/__init__.py.
evaluation_criteria: Must list at least the modules: src/flask/__init__.py, src/flask/json/__init__.py, src/flask/globals.py
Must show the cycle as a closed loop (final module imports the first)
Must identify which import statement(s) close the cycle

fix_applied.expected_solution: Fix approach: Use lazy/deferred imports in flask/json/__init__.py to avoid importing flask.globals at module load time. Apply the fix in src/flask/json/__init__.py (the module that creates the dependency back to the root). Verification: re-running the importer code path must succeed without ImportError.
evaluation_criteria: Must apply a code change that breaks the cycle (e.g. lazy import or import-inside-function)
Must keep public API behavior unchanged (callers still get the expected symbol)
Must include a verification step demonstrating the cycle is resolved
